html:
A jurist and writer of Timbuktu, the best known scholar of the city's golden age. He came from a family of judges and wrote dozens of works on law, grammar and the lives of scholars of the Maliki school of Islamic law.

In 1591 a Moroccan army sent by the Saadi sultan crushed the Songhai Empire at the Battle of Tondibi. Two years later Ahmad Baba and other scholars were arrested and taken to Marrakesh. His library, by his own count about 1,600 books, was lost. In Marrakesh he taught and was widely consulted.

He returned to Timbuktu around 1608. In a well known legal opinion he argued that free Muslims could not be enslaved, whatever their colour. The research centre that keeps the Timbuktu manuscripts is named the Ahmed Baba Institute after him.
